content:
We have carbon NMR data: chemical shifts: 138.76, 131.45 (twice), 130.59 (twice), 121.30, 43.47, 38.60.

We need number of CH3 groups (methyl). Methyl carbons typically appear around 10-30 ppm for aliphatic, but can be higher if attached to electronegative groups. Here we have two aliphatic carbons: 43.47 and 38.60. Those could be CH2 or CH3. Need to determine if they are methyls. Also aromatic carbons are the higher shifts (130-140). So the molecule likely has aromatic ring plus some aliphatic substituents.

We need number of CH3 groups. Could be 0,1,2 etc. Need more info: maybe we can get proton NMR to see methyl signals. Let's request proton NMR.
